rem:transfer-matrix-operator-properties:
Remark Action on the GS ideal, operator algebra, interaction catalogue, and composition rules. The transfer matrix T_{K_1, K_2}(q) acts on the Gröbner--Shirshov-reduced Hecke chain, generates a non-commutative operator algebra under composition, and catalogues every particle interaction together with its \Delta operator and composition rules.

Action on the Gröbner--Shirshov ideal

The transfer matrix acts on the Iwahori--Hecke algebra element a\sigma_i + b (the Gröbner--Shirshov-reduced chain at generator \sigma_i) by left multiplication followed by Hecke reduction:

  T_{K_1, K_2}  \cdot  (a\sigma + b)
   := 
  (c\sigma + d)(a\sigma + b)
  \stackrel{T^2 = (q-q^{-1})T + 1}{\longrightarrow}
  a'\sigma + b'

where:

  a' = ac(q - q^{-1}) + ad + bc,
  \qquad
  b' = ac + bd.

In matrix form:

  \begin{pmatrix} a' \\ b' \end{pmatrix}
  = 
  T_{K_1, K_2}(q)
   \cdot 
  \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix}

The product of k transfer matrices at generator \sigma_i gives the full chain reduction M_i = \prod_{j} T_j(q), and the Markov-traced volume is \hat{V}_i = z \cdot (M_i)_{11} + (M_i)_{21}.

The operator algebra

Transfer matrices compose: if strands K_1, K_2, K_3 cross in sequence at generator \sigma_i, the combined operator is:

  T_{K_1 K_3} \circ T_{K_1 K_2}
  = 
  T_{K_1, K_3}(q) \cdot T_{K_1, K_2}(q)

(matrix multiplication). This is non-commutative — the order of crossings matters.

The Gröbner--Shirshov ideal is the kernel:

  I_i =  \ker\!\left(
    \prod_{j} T_j(q) - M_i(q)
  \right)

The ideal I_i at generator \sigma_i absorbs the terms eliminated by the Hecke relation (T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1). The transfer matrix product M_i(q) is the quotient — the element surviving after modding out I_i.

Interaction catalogue

Every particle interaction corresponds to a transfer matrix. The interaction type is determined by the knot types of the two strands at the crossing:

Nuclear interactions (quark-level, Level 1)

Each quark is an unknot strand of \mathcal{B}_3 (up quark); the strands are distinguished by crossing orientation, not knot type.

Interaction K_1 K_2 T(q) Physical
\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u} unknot, \sigma_i unknot, \sigma_i T_{pp} proton-proton repulsion
\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} unknot, \sigma_i^{-1} unknot, \sigma_i^{-1} T_{nn} neutron-neutron
\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d} unknot, \sigma_i unknot, \sigma_i^{-1} T_{\mathrm{mix}} proton-neutron binding

Electromagnetic interactions (electron-level)

Interaction K_1 K_2 Physical
e-\mathfrak{p} T_{2,3} \mathcal{B}_3 Electron-nucleus Coulomb
e-e T_{2,3} T_{2,3} Electron-electron repulsion
\gamma-e \varnothing T_{2,3} Photon absorption/emission

Photon-electron transfer matrix

The photon (\varnothing, empty knot) crossing with the electron (T_{2,3}, trefoil) gives:

  T_{\gamma e}(q)
  = 
  T_{\varnothing, T_{2,3}}(q)

Since the empty knot has J_{\varnothing}(q) = 1: c_{\gamma e} = J_{T_{2,3}}(q) / J_{T_{2,3}}(q) = 1 and d_{\gamma e} = 0. Therefore:

  T_{\gamma e}(q) =  T_{pp}(q)
  = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q - q^{-1} & 1 \\
    1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix}

The photon-electron transfer matrix is the same as the proton-proton matrix. This is because J_{\varnothing}(q) = 1 (trivial Jones polynomial of the empty knot), so the photon contributes no deformation — the crossing is purely determined by the electron.

Shell transitions as R-I moves

Photon absorption promotes an electron from shell n to shell n+1. In the transfer matrix language, this is a Reidemeister I move on the electron-nucleus Hopf link: a curl is added to the electron trefoil, changing its writhe by \pm 1 but preserving its knot type.

The R-I move at the electron-nucleus junction:

  \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i \cdot \sigma_n

adds one transfer matrix factor T_{\gamma e} to the chain at generator \sigma_i. The energy change is:

  \Delta E_n
  = 
  \hat{V}_i^{(n+1)} - \hat{V}_i^{(n)}
  = 
  z \cdot (T_{\gamma e} \cdot M_i^{(n)})_{11}
  + (T_{\gamma e} \cdot M_i^{(n)})_{21}
  - \hat{V}_i^{(n)}

For hydrogen (A = 1, single electron-proton junction): the transfer matrix at shell n is T_{\gamma e}^n (the n-th power). The energy:

  E_n  \propto  \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n)
  = 
  z \cdot (T_{\gamma e}^n)_{11} + (T_{\gamma e}^n)_{21}

Since T_{\gamma e} has eigenvalues \lambda_{\pm} = \frac{1}{2}\bigl[(q - q^{-1}) \pm \sqrt{(q - q^{-1})^2 + 4}\bigr], the n-th power grows as \lambda_+^n, and the energy scales as:

  E_n  \propto  \lambda_+^n

The energy difference between shells:

  \Delta E_{n \to n+1}
  = 
  \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^{n+1}) - \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n)
  = 
  \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n) \cdot (\lambda_+ - 1)

This gives the photon energy for shell transitions — a geometric series in the eigenvalue \lambda_+ of the photon-electron transfer matrix.

Interaction as Δ operator

Any interaction that changes the crossing type from (K_1, K_2) \to (K_1', K_2') is encoded by the interaction operator:

  \Delta_{K_1 K_2 \to K_1' K_2'}(q)
  = 
  T_{K_1', K_2'}(q) - T_{K_1, K_2}(q)

This is a 2\times2 matrix with polynomial entries in q.

Interaction \Delta operator Physical process
\beta^- decay \Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn} \mathfrak{d} \to \mathfrak{u} crossing change
\beta^+ decay -\Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{pp} \mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{d} crossing change
Photon absorption \Delta_\gamma = T_{\gamma e} (appended) R-I move adds crossing
Pair creation \Delta_{\mathrm{pair}} = T_{ee} - T_{\gamma\gamma} \gamma \to e^+ e^-

For beta decay, \Delta_\beta is universal (beta decay matrix): the same matrix for every nucleus.

For photon absorption, the operator is not a difference but an extension: a new transfer matrix factor T_{\gamma e} is appended to the chain, increasing the color degree by 1.

Composition rules

Sequential interactions (two interactions in sequence at the same generator):

  \Delta_{\mathrm{total}} = \Delta_2 \cdot T_{\mathrm{between}} \cdot \Delta_1
  + \Delta_1 + \Delta_2

Parallel interactions (interactions at different generators):

  \frac{P_{\mathrm{final}}}{P_{\mathrm{initial}}}
  = 
  \prod_{i \in \mathrm{affected}} \frac{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{final}}}{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{initial}}}

The generators factorize — each affected generator contributes independently to the Skein polynomial ratio.
prop:transfer-matrix-identities:
Proposition Transfer matrix identities: T_{pp}T_{nn} = I and T_{pn}^2 = [2]_q^2/4 \cdot I. The three typed transfer matrices satisfy two exact identities in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]).

Statement

(i) T_{pp} \cdot T_{nn} = T_{nn} \cdot T_{pp} = I.

(ii) T_{pn}^2 = \dfrac{[2]_q^2}{4} \cdot I, where [2]_q = q + q^{-1}.

The corollaries — nuclear binding from mixed crossings and the scalar pairing per mixed-crossing pair — are collected in the transfer-matrix-identity corollaries.
rem:transfer-matrix-identities-context:
Remark Corollaries: nuclear binding from mixed crossings and scalar pairing.

Corollaries

Nuclear binding from mixed crossings only. Identity (i) means that adjacent pp and nn crossings cancel in the transfer matrix chain. In the interleaved ground-state ordering, pp crossings (from proton-proton pairs) and nn crossings (from neutron-neutron pairs) contribute zero net effect. All nuclear binding energy arises from the mixed (pn) crossings, whose transfer matrix T_{pn} has trace 0 and determinant -(1 + h^2/4).

Scalar pairing from mixed crossings. Identity (ii) means that every pair of mixed crossings produces a scalar (proportional to I). The binding strength per pair is [2]_q^2/4 = (q + q^{-1})^2/4, which is the square of half the quantum 2-integer. At q_0: [2]_q^2/4 \approx 1.011.
prf:transfer-matrix-identities:
Proof Proof of transfer matrix identities. (i) Direct multiplication. With h = q - q^{-1}:

  \begin{pmatrix} h & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & -h \end{pmatrix}
  =
  \begin{pmatrix} h \cdot 0 + 1 \cdot 1 & h \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot (-h) \\
  1 \cdot 0 + 0 \cdot 1 & 1 \cdot 1 + 0 \cdot (-h) \end{pmatrix}
  =
  \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}.

The (0,1) entry vanishes: h + (-h) = 0. The reverse product T_{nn} \cdot T_{pp} is identical by the same computation.

This is the transfer matrix expression of the Hecke relation: T_{pp} encodes \sigma (crossing coefficient d = 0) and T_{nn} encodes \sigma^{-1} (coefficient d = -h), so T_{pp} \cdot T_{nn} = \sigma \cdot \sigma^{-1} = \mathbf{1}.

(ii) Direct multiplication:

  \begin{pmatrix} h/2 & 1 \\ 1 & -h/2 \end{pmatrix}^2
  =
  \begin{pmatrix} h^2/4 + 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 + h^2/4 \end{pmatrix}.

The diagonal entries are (h/2)(h/2) + 1 \cdot 1 = h^2/4 + 1, and the off-diagonals vanish: (h/2)(1) + 1(-h/2) = 0. Then

  1 + \frac{h^2}{4}
  = 1 + \frac{(q - q^{-1})^2}{4}
  = \frac{4 + q^2 - 2 + q^{-2}}{4}
  = \frac{(q + q^{-1})^2}{4}
  = \frac{[2]_q^2}{4}. \qquad\square
prop:ground-state-ordering:
Proposition The interleaved ordering does not minimise the dilogarithm volume. Let Z protons and N neutrons (A = Z + N) be arranged along the transfer-matrix chain, and let

  \Phi_q = \sum_i \log|\hat{V}_i|

be the quantum dilogarithm volume of that chain. Consider the interleaved, tail-packed arrangement

  \mathrm{ordering}[k]
  =
  \begin{cases}
    1 \text{ (proton)} & k \text{ odd}, \; k < 2Z \\
    0 \text{ (neutron)} & \text{otherwise.}
  \end{cases}

This arrangement does not minimise \Phi_q. Explicitly, at A = 5, Z = 1, N = 4 it is the strict maximiser: the sorted arrangement p\,n\,n\,n\,n satisfies

  \Phi_q(p\,n\,n\,n\,n) < \Phi_q(n\,p\,n\,n\,n)

for every q in an interval containing the aether anchor q_0 \approx 1.10998 and for every Markov parameter lying strictly between the two transfer-matrix eigenvalues, with equality only in the undeformed limit q \to 1.

The eigenvalue relation \lambda_+\lambda_- = -1 for the transfer matrix survives; the ordering claim does not.

Status of the three rules

The proposition previously asserted three rules. An exhaustive sweep of \Phi_q over every \binom{A}{Z} arrangement for A \leq 16, at the experimental (proton) anchor, settles each of them.

(i) Interleaving — refuted for A \geq 4. The interleaved arrangement is the \Phi_q minimiser in 17 of 62 swept cases on the bare-nucleon readout (10 of 62 with the electron tail), and is the strict maximiser in 12 (respectively 8). It is not the ground state.

(ii) Tail packing — refuted. The minimising arrangement head-packs, not tail-packs. At Z = 1 the minimising proton position is A - 5 for every 6 \leq N \leq 15, leaving exactly four neutrons after it and all remaining neutrons before it. For Z \geq 2 the minimiser is an interleaved block at an interior offset with neutron runs on both sides.

(iii) Boundary correction (A \leq 3) — holds at A = 3, fails as stated at A = 2. At A = 3 the sorted arrangement is the exhaustive minimiser, on both readouts and on both sides of Z \leq N. At A = 2 the two arrangements are exactly degenerate on the bare chain — a consequence of the transfer factors commuting, so that the readout sees the crossing coefficients only as a multiset — so sorted does not beat interleaving; and with the electron tail appended, sorted is strictly the worse of the two.

Two readouts, not one

\Phi_q is computed in two inequivalent ways in the corpus: over the bare nucleon chain, and over the nucleon chain with an electron tail appended. The verdicts above are stated for both. They differ only for rule (iii) at A = 2, a case that the production path special-cases and never routes through the ordering at all.

The readout as a two-parameter object

Each transfer factor is T(d) = S + d\,\mathbf{1} for a single fixed matrix S with \mathrm{tr}\, S = q - q^{-1} and \det S = -1. All such factors commute, so the chain product depends on the crossing coefficients only as a multiset, and S^2 = (q-q^{-1})S + \mathbf{1} collapses the product to \alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta S. The vertex volume is therefore

  \hat{V}_i = c_+\mu_+ + c_-\mu_-,
  \qquad
  \mu_\pm = \prod_{j > i}(\lambda_\pm + d_{ij}),

with \lambda_+ = q, \lambda_- = -q^{-1} the roots of the characteristic polynomial and, writing z for the Markov parameter,

  c_+ = \frac{z + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  c_- = \frac{q - z}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  c_+ + c_- = 1 .

The sum is 1 identically in z, and z enters the readout nowhere else.

Independence of the Markov-parameter convention

The two arrangements differ at positions 0 and 1 only, and that comparison collapses to a single identity in which z survives only inside the product c_+c_-:

  \hat{V}_0\hat{V}_1(n\,p\,n\,n\,n) - \hat{V}_0\hat{V}_1(p\,n\,n\,n\,n)
  = 2\,c_+c_-\left(\frac{q + q^{-1}}{2}\right)^{4}\frac{q^6 - 1}{q^3},
  \qquad
  4\,c_+c_- = \frac{4q\,(q - z)(qz + 1)}{(q^2 + 1)^2},

the fourth power being the mixed proton–neutron eigenfactor, which carries no z. For q > 1 every other factor is positive, so the counterexample holds exactly when -q^{-1} < z < q — the Markov parameter strictly between the two eigenvalues. The canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) lies in that window for every q > 1 (since -q^{-1} < 0 < q^3/(q^2+1) < q), so the refutation is a fact about the readout across the entire admissible interval (-q^{-1}, q) rather than an artefact of a particular parameter choice; it degenerates to equality only at q = 1, where the deformation switches off, which is why it holds on a whole interval rather than at a single anchor.

Scope

The A \geq 4 refutation is a structural exclusion: an explicit arrangement with strictly smaller \Phi_q, proved for an interval of q containing the anchor and for every Markov parameter in the window above. The description of the actual minimising family is empirical, covering A \leq 16 only, and no claim is made beyond that range. Which ordering the mass and binding computations should use is a separate question and is not settled here.

rem:ground-state-ordering-derivation:
Remark Ground-state ordering: eigenvalue derivation and verification.

Ground-state ordering: the eigenvalue heuristic and what the sweep found

This remark records the eigenvalue argument that originally motivated the interleaving rule, and the exhaustive search that refuted it.

Transfer matrix eigenvalues

The three transfer matrices (transfer matrix) have eigenvalues determined by the typed crossing operators (typed crossings):

See Table 1.

where h = q - q^{-1}.

Key symmetry: T_{nn} is the q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} mirror of T_{pp}. Their eigenvalues are swapped: \lambda_\pm(T_{nn}) = \lambda_\mp(T_{pp}). The mixed matrix T_{pn} has zero trace and equal-magnitude eigenvalues \pm\sqrt{1 + h^2/4} \approx \pm 1.005.

The heuristic

Each T_{pp} contributes dominant eigenvalue +q \approx 1.110 (growth). Each T_{nn} contributes +q^{-1} \approx 0.901 (decay). The interleaved arrangement alternates growth and decay factors, which suggests destructive interference driving |\hat{V}_i| below 1 at most generators, whereas a sorted chain front-loads pure growth. Since T_{pn} has zero trace, its contributions were expected to average to zero over many chain steps, making the mixed crossings neutral spacers between the binding T_{nn} and anti-binding T_{pp} contributions.

The exhaustive sweep below refutes this heuristic.

What the exhaustive sweep found

\Phi_q was evaluated over every \binom{A}{Z} arrangement for each (Z, N) with Z \leq N and A \leq 16, at the experimental aether anchor, on both the bare-nucleon chain and the chain with the electron tail appended.

The interleaved, tail-packed arrangement is the minimiser in a minority of cases and the strict maximiser in a comparable number. At A = 5, Z = 1 it is the strict worst of all five arrangements on both readouts, while the sorted arrangement — which the rule reserves for A \leq 3 — is the minimiser. The excess neutrons of the minimising arrangement head-pack rather than tail-pack. Full tallies and the proved counterexample are in the proposition.

Why the heuristic failed

The transfer factors are T(d) = S + d\,\mathbf{1} for a single fixed matrix S, so they all commute: the chain product at a position depends on the crossing coefficients only as a multiset, and there is no "alternation" for the readout to see. What looks like a growth/decay interference pattern at the level of individual matrices is, at the level of the readout, a product of eigenfactors whose ordering is immaterial. The only thing that varies between arrangements is which multiset sits at which position — and the resulting \Phi_q is not extremised by alternation.

This also explains an exact degeneracy the heuristic cannot account for: at A = 3, Z = 2 the arrangements ppn and pnp have identical \Phi_q on the bare chain.

Connection to the Gram matrix

The transfer matrix eigenvalues are the Gram matrix entries in disguise: \lambda_+(T_{pp}) = q and \lambda_+(T_{nn}) = q^{-1} are the braiding eigenvalues from the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0. That identification is unaffected by the refutation; only the claim that a particular arrangement extremises \Phi_q does not apply.

Scalability

For A > 16 exhaustive search over \binom{A}{Z} arrangements was not attempted, and no closed-form rule for the minimiser is available. The sweep's minimising family — an interleaved block at an interior offset, with the excess neutrons split between a head run and a four-neutron tail — is an empirical description over A \leq 16, not a derived construction.
prop:skein-generation:
Proposition The skein module of the 3-sphere is free on the unknot. Let R = \mathbb{Q}(a, q) and let \mathrm{Sk}(S^3) be the skein module of oriented links in S^3 over R: the R-module spanned by isotopy classes of oriented links, modulo the HOMFLYPT skein relation

  a\, L_+ - a^{-1} L_- = (q - q^{-1})\, L_0

for every triple (L_+, L_-, L_0) of links that differ only at one crossing. Then \mathrm{Sk}(S^3) is free of rank one, spanned by the unknot U:

  [L] = P_L(a, q)\,[U]

for every oriented link L, where P_L \in R is the HOMFLYPT polynomial normalised by P_U = 1. In particular every link, and so every hadron configuration of rem:hadron-operations, has a terminal skein resolution: a finite reduction of L to a multiple of U.

The specialisation a = 1 is the relation L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1}) L_0 of the corpus's Hecke–skein convention, and P_L is then the Conway polynomial in z = q - q^{-1}. At a = q every P_L equals 1, so that specialisation carries no information about L. The reading of this resolution in terms of torus knots, the Hopf link and hadron masses is in rem:skein-generation-hadron-reading.
prf:skein-generation:
Proof Proof of Skein generation. Spanning. Fix a diagram of L with base points on each component and order the crossings. Changing a crossing replaces L_\pm by L_\mp at the cost of a multiple of L_0, which has one fewer crossing; after finitely many changes the diagram is a stack of unknotted, unlinked components (a descending diagram), which is an unlink. Induction on the number of crossings, then on the number of crossings that must be changed, writes [L] as an R-combination of unlinks. For the unlink of c components, apply the relation to a one-crossing kink of one component: L_+ = L_- = the unlink of c components and L_0 is the unlink of c + 1 components, so (a - a^{-1})\,[U^{\sqcup c}] = (q - q^{-1})\,[U^{\sqcup (c+1)}], hence [U^{\sqcup (c+1)}] = \tfrac{a - a^{-1}}{q - q^{-1}}\,[U^{\sqcup c}] in R. So [U] spans.

Freeness. The HOMFLYPT polynomial exists as an isotopy invariant satisfying the relation with P_U = 1 [lickorish1997], so [L] \mapsto P_L is a well-defined R-linear map \mathrm{Sk}(S^3) \to R sending [U] to 1. Hence [U] is not torsion and \mathrm{Sk}(S^3) = R\,[U] is free of rank one, with [L] = P_L [U]. \square
lem:skein-mass-from-linking:
Lemma Mass functional on a Skein resolution: linking-energy plus constituent volume. Evaluating the mass functional \mathfrak{m} on the terminal Skein resolution of a hadron H gives

  \mathfrak{m}(H)
  = 
  Q(q) \cdot \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}})
  +
  \sum_{i=1}^{n}
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K_i)}{\hbar_q^{2}},

where the first term is the binding energy from linking and the second is the constituent mass (zero for torus-knot constituents), Q(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] is the Skein polynomial of the linking configuration, and \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}.
prf:skein-mass-from-linking:
Proof Proof of the Skein-resolution mass formula. Evaluating the mass functional \mathfrak{m} on the Skein resolution of H gives:

  \mathfrak{m}(H)
  = 
  \underbrace{Q(q) \cdot \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}})}_{\text{binding energy (from linking)}}
  + 
  \underbrace{\sum_{i=1}^{n}
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K_i)}{\hbar_q^{2}}}_{\text{constituent mass (zero for torus knots)}}

where Q(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] is the Skein polynomial of the linking configuration and \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}.

For hadrons composed entirely of fundamental (torus-knot) constituents, \mathrm{Vol}(K_i) = 0 for all i, so the entire inertial mass arises from the linking topology:

  \mathfrak{m}(H) =  Q(q) \cdot \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}).

\square
rem:skein-generation-hadron-reading:
Remark Fundamental knots, the Hopf link and the hadron reading of skein generation. In the particle dictionary, a knot type is fundamental if it is the unknot or a torus knot: the unknot (neutrino), the trefoil 3_1, the cinquefoil 5_1 (tau) and the torus (p, 2) family. The electron is not among them: it is \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link, with the trefoil \sigma_0^3 \in B_2 kept as a backup candidate. Every fundamental knot has \mathrm{Vol}(K) = 0, but not conversely: satellite knots, including composites such as 3_1 \# 3_1, also have volume zero. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} is read as the binding operation, and a hadron H \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} as a configuration of fundamental knots joined by Hopf links.

prop:skein-generation resolves every such H to P_H(a, q)\,[U]. In particular the fundamental knots and the Hopf link generate the skein module, but so does the unknot alone, and the resolution records linking only through the polynomial P_H.

The mass reading takes the form \mathfrak{m}(H) = Q(q)\, \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) + \sum_i \mathrm{Vol}(K_i)/\hbar_q^2 of lem:skein-mass-from-linking, so that a hadron built from fundamental constituents takes its whole mass from linking. That step needs a specialisation in which the Hopf link is not identified with the unknot. The specialization a = q, where the skein relation reads q L_+ - q^{-1} L_- = (q - q^{-1}) L_0, forces P_L = 1 for every link and identifies the Hopf link with the unknot, so it does not supply that step. At a = 1 the Hopf link resolves to (q - q^{-1})\,[U] with the orientation for which its crossings are positive, and the split unlink to 0, so linking is visible there. Which specialisation the mass reading uses is not fixed by the proposition.
lem:nucleon-borromean-topology: Lemma Nucleon Borromean topology and Hopf-link binding. The proton and neutron are Borromean configurations (6_2^3) of three quark vortices. They are internally bound by Hopf links \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}. Since \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) = 0, the mass contribution arises entirely from the Skein functional.
prf:nucleon-borromean-topology: Proof Proof of nucleon Borromean topology. The proton and neutron are each modelled as a Borromean-ring configuration (6_2^3) of three quark vortices. They are bound internally by Hopf links \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} representing the strong color-exchange interaction. The Hopf link is a torus link with \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) = 0. Its mass contribution therefore arises entirely from the Skein functional, not from hyperbolic volume. \square
lem:pair-skein-mass-formula:
Lemma Pair Skein mass and crossing-by-crossing recursion. The Borromean braid of a nucleon with quarks (q_1, q_2, q_3) contributes a pair Skein mass at each color-exchange crossing:

  \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q)
  =
  \frac{q\mu_a +  q^{-1}\mu_b}
       {q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}.

The total nucleon mass is:

  m_N
  =
  \mathcal{S}_{q_1 q_2}(q)
  + \mathcal{S}_{q_1 q_3}(q)
  + \mathcal{S}_{q_2 q_3}(q).

The denominator q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2} is the reciprocal of the half-argument weight 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) = \sqrt q/(q+1) rather than the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1). Substituting z = q^3/(q^2+1) directly is not a valid move, because the crossing-pair trace must be re-derived under that parameter.
prf:pair-skein-mass-formula:
Proof Proof of the pair Skein mass formula. The Borromean braid of a nucleon with quarks (q_1, q_2, q_3) has six crossings organised into three crossing pairs. Each pair corresponds to a color-exchange channel. At each pair involving quarks of species a and b, a double application of the Skein relation yields the pair Skein mass

  \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q)
  =
  \frac{q\mu_a +  q^{-1}\mu_b}
       {q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}},

where \mu_a is the dressed quark Skein mass of species a. This \mu_a represents the mass contribution of a single quark strand including its strong-field dressing from the Hopf-link interaction with the color background. The total nucleon mass is the sum over the three crossing pairs:

  m_N
  =
  \mathcal{S}_{q_1 q_2}(q)
  + \mathcal{S}_{q_1 q_3}(q)
  + \mathcal{S}_{q_2 q_3}(q).

The denominator q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2} is not derived above: it corresponds to the half-argument weight 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) = \sqrt q/(q+1) rather than the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1). \square
prop:flavor-split-aether:
Proposition Closed and factored forms of the aether flavor split. For every nonzero q,

  \frac{(q - 1)^2 \, (1 - q^{-4})}{3}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q}{3},

where \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}, h_q = q - q^{-1} and [2]_q = q + q^{-1}.
prf:flavor-split-aether:
Proof Proof of the aether-pure flavor split formula. Step 5 proves the identity: dividing (4) by 3 gives it, and it holds for every nonzero q. Steps 1 to 4 and 6 show how its two sides arise as the aether formula for (m_n - m_p)/M_N, under the pair-Skein formula and the ansatz of Step 2. Those steps are not needed for the identity.

Step 1 (Pair-Skein difference, exact).

Apply Pair Skein mass and crossing-by-crossing recursion to the Borromean baryon braids of the proton (\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) and neutron (\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}). This gives the exact relation:

  m_n - m_p
  \;=\;
  \frac{q + q^{-1}}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}} (\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}})
  \;=\;
  [2]_q \cdot z_{\text{mkv}} \cdot (\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}),

where z_{\text{mkv}} = (q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})^{-1} = \sqrt q/(q+1) is the half-argument skein weight inherited from the pair-Skein formula. Steps 1 and 3 depend on that specific denominator: at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) the product [2]_q z equals q^2, and substituting z is not valid without re-deriving the pair-Skein crossing relation at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Dividing by \mu_{\text{avg}} = (\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + \mu_{\mathfrak{d}})/2:

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;=\;
  [2]_q \cdot z_{\text{mkv}} \cdot
  \frac{\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}. \tag{1}

Step 2 (Aether ansatz for the per-quark split).

The aether prescription for (\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}})/\mu_{\text{avg}} is:

  \frac{\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;\approx\;
  h_q^2 \cdot \frac{\hbar_q}{\sqrt{q}},
  \qquad
  h_q = q - q^{-1},
  \quad
  \hbar_q = \frac{q - 1}{q}. \tag{2}

This is the minimal aether-atom combination satisfying three conditions: (a) Bar-involution antisymmetry under q \mapsto q^{-1} (consistent with the antisymmetry of the splitting under flavor exchange \mathfrak{u} \leftrightarrow \mathfrak{d}). (b) Leading order (q-1)^3 at the classical limit. (c) Numerical agreement to -0.13\% at the proton-anchored q = q_0.

Scope of Step 2. Equation (2) is a phenomenological ansatz rather than a derived identity: Condition (c) chooses the form because it agrees with experiment, which is selection against the target. Conditions (a) and (b) do not single it out:

  • (b) holds: the right-hand side is 4(q-1)^3 + O((q-1)^4).
  • (a) does not hold as stated. Writing f(q) = h_q^2\,\hbar_q/\sqrt{q}, one finds f(q^{-1}) = -q^2 f(q), so f is antisymmetric under q \mapsto q^{-1} only up to the factor q^2 (checked symbolically).

Everything downstream of (2) therefore inherits a fitted input, and no derivation is on record. One class of derived objects is excluded. Suppose the nucleon masses are additive over strands, m_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} and m_{\mathfrak{n}} = \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + 2\mu_{\mathfrak{d}}, and that m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_{\mathfrak{n}} is a nonzero integer power of q, as for the pivot ratio q^{\pm 2} that the restricted quantum trace gives on the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) commutant. Then, with t = \sqrt{q}, the per-quark split is c\,(t^m - 1)/(t^m + 1) for a nonzero rational c and an integer m \ge 1. This vanishes to first order at q = 1, while the right-hand side of (2) vanishes to third order, so the two never agree, and the ansatz also fails bar-parity symmetry. The exclusion says nothing about non-additive strand rules or about objects that break U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) symmetry.

Step 3 (Algebraic identity tying the equivalent forms).

  h_q \cdot z_{\text{mkv}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}
  \;=\;
  q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}
  \;=\;
  z_0,

and \hbar_q \cdot \sqrt{q} = (q - 1)/\sqrt{q} = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2} = z_0. So h_q \cdot z_{\text{mkv}} = z_0 = \hbar_q \cdot \sqrt{q}. The first equality is specific to z_{\text{mkv}} = (q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})^{-1}: for the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the product h_q z \approx 0.1281 at q_0 differs from q_0^{1/2} - q_0^{-1/2} \approx 0.1044. This gives the chain of equivalent forms:

  h_q^2 \cdot \frac{\hbar_q}{\sqrt{q}}
  \;=\;
  h_q^2 \cdot \frac{z_0}{q}
  \;=\;
  h_q^3 \cdot \frac{z_{\text{mkv}}}{q}
  \;=\;
  \frac{h_q^2 \cdot (q-1)}{q^{3/2}}.

Step 4 (Factored Hecke-atom form for the nucleon split).

Substituting (2) into (1):

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;=\;
  [2]_q \cdot z_{\text{mkv}} \cdot h_q^2 \cdot \frac{\hbar_q}{\sqrt{q}}.

Using z_{\text{mkv}} = z_0 / h_q = (\hbar_q \cdot \sqrt{q})/h_q (from Step 3), this collapses to:

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;=\;
  [2]_q \cdot h_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q \cdot \frac{\hbar_q \sqrt{q}}{h_q \sqrt{q}}
  \;=\;
  \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q. \tag{3}

Step 5 (Closed-form polynomial identity).

Substituting \hbar_q = (q-1)/q, h_q = (q^2-1)/q, and [2]_q = (q^2+1)/q into (3):

  \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q-1)^2}{q^2} \cdot \frac{q^2 - 1}{q} \cdot \frac{q^2 + 1}{q}
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q-1)^2 \, (q^2 - 1)(q^2 + 1)}{q^4}
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q-1)^2 \, (q^4 - 1)}{q^4}
  \;=\;
  (q-1)^2 \cdot (1 - q^{-4}). \tag{4}

Step 6 (Conversion to per-nucleon form).

The per-quark mass averages to the per-nucleon mass via M_N = 3 \mu_{\text{avg}} (one quark mass per strand of the baryon braid, summed over three strands). Therefore:

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{M_N}
  \;=\;
  \frac{m_n - m_p}{3 \mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q}{3}
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q-1)^2 \, (1 - q^{-4})}{3}. \tag{5}
conj:flavor-split-aether-mass:
Conjecture The nucleon mass split equals the aether flavor-split formula. Let M_N = (m_{\mathfrak{p}} + m_{\mathfrak{n}})/2 and \mu_{\text{avg}} = (\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + \mu_{\mathfrak{d}})/2. The nucleon mass split is given by the aether flavor-split formula:

  \frac{m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}}}{M_N}
  \;\approx\;
  \frac{(q - 1)^2 \, (1 - q^{-4})}{3},
  \qquad
  \frac{m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}}}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;\approx\;
  \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q .

Here \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}, h_q = q - q^{-1} and [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. By the closed and factored forms of the aether flavor split, the first right-hand side is the second divided by 3. The two displayed claims are therefore equivalent exactly when M_N = 3\mu_{\text{avg}}, which is the additive-strand relation of Step 6 of that proposition's proof; the conjecture asserts the first claim, and the second follows from it under that relation.

Status. The derivation sketch in the proof of that proposition (Steps 1, 2 and 6) obtains this formula from the pair Skein formula and an ansatz for the per-quark split (\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}})/\mu_{\text{avg}}. The ansatz was chosen partly because it agrees with experiment, and no derivation of it is on record. For nucleon masses that are additive over strands with a mass ratio that is a nonzero power of q, it is excluded: every such split vanishes to first order at q = 1, while the ansatz vanishes to third order. The pair Skein formula itself uses the half-argument denominator q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2} rather than the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1).

prop:corrected-markov-trace:
Proposition Markov trace of \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0. The Markov trace of the braid word \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0 (whose closure is the Hopf link) is hz^2 + z, not z^3. The value z^3 comes from applying the Markov property to a generator that is not of maximal index, which the property does not allow.

Statement

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0) = h z^2 + z

where z = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0) is the Markov parameter and h = q - q^{-1}.
prf:corrected-markov-trace:
Proof Proof of corrected markov trace. Use the properties of the Markov trace (Jones–Markov trace): it is linear, satisfies \mathrm{tr}_M(ab) = \mathrm{tr}_M(ba) and \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, and satisfies \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) only when x \in H_n(q), that is, when \sigma_n is the largest generator in the word and does not occur in x.

  1. By cyclicity, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0^2 \sigma_1).

  2. Here \sigma_0^2 \in H_2(q) and \sigma_1 is the largest generator, so the Markov property gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0^2 \sigma_1) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0^2).

  3. By the Hecke relation \sigma_0^2 = h\sigma_0 + 1, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0^2) = hz + 1.

Therefore \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0) = z(hz + 1) = hz^2 + z. \square

The value z^3 is obtained by peeling the outer \sigma_0 with the Markov property. That step is invalid, because \sigma_0 is not the largest generator of \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0.

prop:frobenius-gram-matrix:
Proposition Frobenius Gram matrix and dual construction in H_3(q).

Gram matrix (symbolic in q)

Proposition. Let h = q - q^{-1} and let z = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0) be the Markov parameter, so that by the three-strand Markov trace identity the longest-word trace is e := \mathrm{tr}_M(e^-) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0) = hz^2 + z. The 6 \times 6 Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) over the normal-form basis \{\gamma, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+, L_-, e^-\} of H_3(q) is

  G
  =
  \begin{pmatrix}
    1     & z     & z     & z^2     & z^2     & hz^2+z \\
    z     & hz+1  & z^2   & hz^2+z  & hz^2+z  & g_{15} \\
    z     & z^2   & hz+1  & hz^2+z  & hz^2+z  & g_{15} \\
    z^2   & hz^2+z & hz^2+z & g_{15} & g_{34} & g_{35} \\
    z^2   & hz^2+z & hz^2+z & g_{34} & g_{15} & g_{35} \\
    hz^2+z & g_{15} & g_{15} & g_{35} & g_{35} & g_{55}
  \end{pmatrix}

where, substituting e = hz^2 + z into each reduced basis product:

  • g_{15} = h\,e + z^2 = (h^2 + 1)z^2 + hz (from \sigma_0 \cdot e^- = he^- + L_- and \sigma_1 \cdot e^- = L_+ L_+ = he^- + L_+)
  • g_{34} = h\,e + hz + 1 = (hz + 1)^2 (from L_+ \cdot L_- = he^- + h\sigma_0 + \gamma)
  • g_{35} = h^2 e + 2hz^2 + z = (h^3 + 2h)z^2 + (h^2 + 1)z (from L_+ \cdot e^- = h^2e^- + hL_+ + hL_- + \sigma_1)
  • g_{55} = (h^3+h)e + 2h^2z^2 + 2hz + 1 = (h^4 + 3h^2)z^2 + (h^3 + 3h)z + 1 (from e^- \cdot e^- = (h^3+h)e^- + h^2L_+ + h^2L_- + h\sigma_1 + h\sigma_0 + \gamma)

The matrix is symmetric (G_{ij} = G_{ji}, by cyclicity of the Markov trace), with determinant \det G(q, z) = -(z - q)^5(qz + 1)^5\bigl((q^2 + 1)z - q^3\bigr)(q^3 z + qz + 1)/q^8. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2 + 1), the (1^3) Wedderburn block carries y_{(1^3)} = 0 symbolically, so that block lies in the radical of the form, \det G = 0 identically, and G^{-1} does not exist on H_3(q) (the induced pairing is non-degenerate on the 5-dimensional Temperley--Lieb quotient \mathrm{TL}_3(q)). Any statement about the signature must name its pairing. On the bilinear pairing \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) above, the spectrum at q_0 is (-0.75270211,\ 0,\ +0.75270211^{\times 3},\ +4.23033923). On the star pairing \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j^*) — where the Hecke star T_w^* = T_{w^{-1}} exchanges L_+ \leftrightarrow L_- on this basis — the form is positive semidefinite of signature (5,0,1). An indefinite signature appears only on the untwisted bilinear pairing; what survives both pairings at z = q^3/(q^2 + 1) is the single null direction.

The Markov-trace computation of the NF basis elements, the operator-identification via the Frobenius dual, and the annihilation identity e^- \cdot e^+ = \gamma are collected in the Frobenius Gram-matrix context.
def:frobenius-dual-h3:
Definition Frobenius dual K^\vee in H_3(q). Let G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) be the Gram matrix of the Frobenius pairing on the NF basis \{b_i\} of H_3(q) (Frobenius Gram matrix), read at z = q^3/(q^2+1) on the quotient H_3/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \cong \mathrm{TL}_3, where the induced pairing is non-degenerate. For a state K = \sum_i c_i b_i in NF, the Frobenius dual is the unique element K^\vee \in H_3(q) satisfying \langle K^\vee, b_j \rangle_F = c_j for all j. Explicitly:

  K^\vee = \sum_{i,j} c_i (G^{-1})_{ij} b_j.
rem:frobenius-dual-h3-remark:
Remark Degeneracy on H_3 and existence of the Frobenius dual. On H_3 itself the Gram matrix is degenerate: \det G = 0 identically, the (1^3) block being the radical of the Markov trace (MarkovGramDegenerate.lean). Non-degeneracy therefore holds on H_3/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_3 and not on H_3.

The dual exists and is unique by non-degeneracy of G on that quotient: the pairing \langle K^\vee, b_j \rangle_F = \sum_{i,k} c_i (G^{-1})_{ik} G_{kj} = \sum_i c_i \delta_{ij} = c_j follows from G^{-1} G = I.

Remark NF Markov-trace computation, operator identification via the dual, and the annihilation identity. The Frobenius self-duality A \cong A^\vee induces a concrete bilinear form on H_3(q) via the Markov trace. The Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) over the NF basis encodes all interaction pairings, and its inverse G^{-1} gives the explicit dual construction K^\vee = \sum_{i,j} c_i (G^{-1})_{ij} b_j.

G is singular on H_3 — read G^{-1} on the Temperley–Lieb quotient. Writing G^{-1} on all of H_3(q) presupposes \det G \neq 0. Every use of G^{-1} and of K^\vee below should be read on that 5-dimensional quotient (\sum \dim^2 = C_3 = 5), not on the 6-dimensional H_3.

thm:em-spectral-completeness:
Theorem Two-strand spectral completeness over a commutative ring R. Setup (commutative ring of coefficients). Throughout, the categorical structure is R-enriched over

  R \;=\; \mathbb{Z}\bigl[q^{\pm 1/2},\, (q - q^{-1})^{-1}\bigr].

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a rigid braided monoidal category R-enriched with self-dual fundamental object A of categorical dimension \dim_q A = [2]_q \in R, and \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-mod} the fibre functor.

Theorem (two-strand spectral completeness). The Frobenius R-algebra E := \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A \otimes A) is a free R-module of rank 2 with the following structure.

  1. There exist exactly two non-zero central idempotents e_+, e_- \in E with e_+ + e_- = \mathrm{id}_{A \otimes A} and e_+ \cdot e_- = 0.
  2. Each e_\pm projects onto a simple summand: 
      A \otimes A \;\cong\; V_+ \oplus V_-,
  \qquad e_\pm A^{\otimes 2} = V_\pm.
    The summand V_- is canonically isomorphic to the unit object \mathbf{1} — a singlet of R-rank one.
  3. In the unimodular half-power normalisation (c_{A,A} - q^{1/2})(c_{A,A} + q^{-1/2}) = 0, the braiding decomposes as 
      c_{A,A} \;=\; q^{1/2}\, e_+ \;-\; q^{-1/2}\, e_-,
    and \{q^{1/2},\, -q^{-1/2}\} are the only eigenvalues of c_{A,A} on A \otimes A. Equivalently, the rescaled generator \sigma := q^{1/2}\,c_{A,A} = q\,e_+ - q^{-1}\,e_- satisfies the monograph's integer-power Iwahori--Hecke relation \sigma^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma + 1 with eigenvalues \{q,\, -q^{-1}\} and identical central idempotents e_\pm.
  4. (Trace completeness.) With \dim_q V_+ = [3]_q and \dim_q V_- = 1, the normalised categorical traces of the idempotents 
      w_\pm \;:=\; \frac{\mathrm{tr}_q(e_\pm)}{\mathrm{tr}_q(\mathrm{id}_{A \otimes A})}
  \;=\; \frac{\dim_q V_\pm}{[2]_q^{\,2}}
    satisfy w_+ + w_- = 1, because [3]_q + 1 = [2]_q^{\,2}.
prf:em-spectral-completeness:
Proof Proof of em spectral completeness. Proof. The braiding eigenvalue extraction (eigenvalue extraction) shows that c_{A,A} satisfies the Hecke minimal polynomial

  (c_{A,A} - q^{1/2})(c_{A,A} + q^{-1/2}) \;=\; 0

in E. The two eigenvalues q^{1/2}, -q^{-1/2} are distinct (their difference q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2} is a unit in R), so the minimal polynomial splits over R and Bezout produces orthogonal idempotents

  e_- \;=\; \frac{q^{1/2} \cdot \mathrm{id} - c_{A,A}}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}
      \;=\; \frac{q \cdot \mathrm{id} - \sigma}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  e_+ \;=\; \mathrm{id} - e_-
      \;=\; \frac{\sigma + q^{-1} \cdot \mathrm{id}}{q + q^{-1}},

where \sigma := q^{1/2}\,c_{A,A} satisfies the integer-power Hecke quadratic (\sigma - q)(\sigma + q^{-1}) = 0, i.e. \sigma^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma + 1, over the subring \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}, (q + q^{-1})^{-1}] \subset R. These idempotents are central in E since c_{A,A} (or \sigma) generates the centraliser of the diagonal R-action by Schur--Weyl-Hecke duality. Statement (2) follows from H_2(R, q) \cong E being free of rank 2 over R: E has at most two simple summands, and e_\pm realise them. The singlet identification V_- \cong \mathbf{1} is the standard Schur-functor decomposition A \otimes A = S^2 A \oplus \Lambda^2 A with \Lambda^2 A \cong \mathbf{1} when A is the fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2). Statement (4) follows from (1) and (2): the categorical trace is additive, so \mathrm{tr}_q(e_+) + \mathrm{tr}_q(e_-) = \mathrm{tr}_q(\mathrm{id}_{A \otimes A}) = (\dim_q A)^2 = [2]_q^{\,2}, and \mathrm{tr}_q(e_\pm) = \dim_q V_\pm with \dim_q V_+ = [3]_q, \dim_q V_- = 1. This is the n = 2 case of the Wedderburn trace identity with multiplicities 1. The squared form (\dim_q V_\pm)^2/[2]_q! does not sum to 1: it gives ([3]_q^2 + 1)/[2]_q, which is 5 at q = 1. \square
prop:borromean-markov-trace-closed-form:
Proposition Borromean Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6)/(h^2 + 4). The Markov trace of the Borromean braid \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_2)^3 on H_3(q), evaluated via the Jones polynomial of the Borromean rings \mathcal{B}_3, admits the exact closed form

  \boxed{\;\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}, q)
  \;=\;
  \frac{4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6}{h^2 + 4},
  \;\;}

where h = q - q^{-1} and h^2 + 4 = [2]_q^2.

Structural significance for the mass formula

The h^2 = 0 result separates the proton-mass h-dependence into clean layers:

Factor in F_{\mathrm{Bor}} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) \cdot [3]_q! / q^3 h^2 coefficient Source
\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) 0 per-partition cancellation (this proposition)
[3]_q! = (h^2 + 3)\sqrt{h^2 + 4} 11/4 algebraic (q-factorial)
q^3 (denominator) 9/8 algebraic (q = (h + \sqrt{h^2+4})/2)
F_{\mathrm{Bor}} (combined) 19/2 11/4 and 9/8 via division

The exact vanishing of the h^2 term in the trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}, q) is an algebraic property of the Borromean rings' Jones polynomial evaluation. In the context of the mass formula, this forces any h^2 dependence in the overall amplitude F_{\mathrm{Bor}} to arise strictly from the normalization factor [3]_q! / q^3.
rem:borromean-colored-jones-habiro-prior:
Remark Prior art: Habiro's coloured Jones formula for the Borromean rings. Habiro computes the Kauffman-bracket invariant of the Borromean rings with each component coloured by an element of the skein module of the solid torus. In the natural basis \{e_n\}, where e_n corresponds to the (n+1)-dimensional irreducible representation of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), the value \langle e_l, e_m, e_n\rangle is a finite sum over 0 \le i \le \min(l,m,n) of powers of (a - a^{-1}) times ratios of quantum factorials, symmetric in l, m, n [habiro2000, \S 3, p. 37]. In his modified basis \{R'_n\} the same invariant is diagonal: it is (a - a^{-1})^n\,[2n+1]!/[n]! when l = m = n and 0 otherwise [habiro2000, Prop. 7.1, p. 41].

The closed form of the Borromean Markov trace is the uncoloured case, so this is the published all-colours version of the same invariant, and Prop. 7.1 is a precise locator for the corpus's citations of this key. The paper works in the Kauffman variable a and its own normalisation; it does not compute the Markov trace in H_3(q), so matching the two at the fundamental colour needs the change of variables and framing to be checked first.
prf:borromean-markov-trace-closed-form:
Proof Proof of borromean markov trace closed form. The Jones polynomial of the Borromean rings is [murasugi1996]:

  V(\mathcal{B}_3, t)
  = -t^{-3} + 3t^{-2} - 2t^{-1} + 4 - 2t + 3t^2 - t^3.

Setting t = q^2 and introducing u := q^2 + q^{-2}, this becomes a polynomial in u:

  V = -u^3 + 3u^2 + u - 2.

For a 3-component link, the Markov trace is \mathrm{tr}_M = V / [2]_q^2 where [2]_q^2 = (q + q^{-1})^2 = u + 2. Polynomial long division yields:

  \frac{V}{u + 2}
  = -u^2 + 5u - 9 + \frac{16}{u + 2}.

Substituting u = h^2 + 2 (where h = q - q^{-1}, so q^2 + q^{-2} = h^2 + 2):

  \mathrm{tr}_M
  = -(h^2 + 2)^2 + 5(h^2 + 2) - 9 + \frac{16}{h^2 + 4}
  = \frac{4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6}{h^2 + 4}.

\square

The h-expansion (purely even)

Taylor-expanding around h = 0:

  \mathrm{tr}_M
  = 1
    + \underbrace{0}_{\text{no } h^2}
    \cdot h^2
    - \underbrace{\frac{3}{4}}_{h^4} \cdot h^4
    - \underbrace{\frac{1}{16}}_{h^6} \cdot h^6
    + \underbrace{\frac{1}{64}}_{h^8} \cdot h^8
    + \cdots

The series is purely even in h (the numerator and denominator are both even polynomials in h). The higher-order coefficients follow a geometric tail from the remainder term 16/(h^2 + 4).

The h^2 coefficient is exactly zero

The vanishing of the h^2 term is a non-trivial cancellation: the numerator HAS an h^2 coefficient (+1), but the denominator's h^2 coefficient (+1) cancels it exactly:

  \frac{4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6}{4 + h^2}
  = \frac{(4 + h^2) + (-3h^4 - h^6)}{4 + h^2}
  = 1 + \frac{-3h^4 - h^6}{h^2 + 4}.

The first non-trivial correction appears at h^4 with coefficient -3/4: the first topological invariant of the Borromean linking structure — the part of the Jones polynomial that distinguishes \mathcal{B}_3 from the trivial 3-component unlink.

Per-representation decomposition and exact h^2 budget

The three irreps of S_3 / H_3(q) contribute distinctly to the Frobenius expansion \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda.

Convention note. Two distinct Markov-trace normalisations are in use for H_3(q), and they have different Wenzl weights and different per-partition budgets:

  1. the Jones-closure normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M = V_{\mathrm{Jones}} / [2]_q^{\,c-1} — the convention of the closed form above — with weights y_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3, y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2, y_{(1^3)} = 0 identically (Closed-form Jones/Temperley–Lieb weights on H_3(q) (Borromean Jones polynomial));
  2. the Wenzl-bridge / Ocneanu normalisation (used by the formal derivation), whose weights are all non-zero and whose trace value on \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} differs from the closed form above (e.g. 0.91926 vs 0.93917 at q = 1.3; that witness records lean_form_matches: false).

An earlier revision of this section tabulated the bridge-convention budget (5/128, -20/128, 15/128) without labelling the convention — those numbers decompose the bridge trace, not the closed form above. Both budgets sum to zero (each trace separately has h^2 = 0), which masked the mismatch.

In the Jones-closure convention used here, the per-partition decomposition is:

  • \lambda = (3) [trivial, dim 1]: \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1 exactly for all q (writhe-zero braid, trivial eigenvalue q^0 = 1); weight y_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3. Per-partition h^2 coefficient of y_{(3)} \cdot \chi^{(3)}: \;+1/8.

  • \lambda = (1^3) [sign, dim 1]: \chi^{(1^3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1 exactly (writhe-zero, sign eigenvalue (-q^{-1})^0 = 1); weight y_{(1^3)} = 0 identically — the Jones polynomial factors through Temperley–Lieb, which annihilates the 3-row partition. Per-partition h^2 coefficient: \;0.

  • \lambda = (2,1) [standard, dim 2]: The only non-abelian irrep, with exact rational character

      \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  = \frac{-q^{12} + 3q^{10} - 3q^8 + 4q^6 - 3q^4 + 3q^2 - 1}{q^6}
  \;=\; 2 - 3h^4 - h^6;

    weight y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2. ALL correction terms (h^4, h^6, \ldots) of \mathrm{tr}_M originate from this partition alone. Per-partition h^2 coefficient of y_{(2,1)} \cdot \chi^{(2,1)}: \;-1/8.

The h^2 budget is exact:

  \underbrace{\frac{1}{8}}_{(3)}
  \;+\; \underbrace{\left(-\frac{1}{8}\right)}_{(2,1)}
  \;+\; \underbrace{0}_{(1^3)}
  \;=\; 0.

(For the record, the bridge-convention budget is (5/128, -20/128, 15/128), also summing to zero — but it decomposes the bridge-normalised trace, a different functional.)

Vanishing of h^2: universal identity + Borromean symmetry

The cancellation follows from two independent facts:

Fact 1 (universal). The Markov trace normalization \sum_\lambda y_\lambda(q) \cdot d_\lambda = 1 holds identically in q. Differentiating twice in h at h = 0:

  \sum_\lambda \bigl[h^2\text{-coeff of } y_\lambda\bigr] \cdot d_\lambda = 0.

This is a knot-independent identity — it constrains the Wenzl weights regardless of which braid is traced.

Fact 2 (Borromean-specific). The braid \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_2)^3 maps under \pi\colon B_3 \to S_3 to (s_1 s_2)^3 = (1\,2\,3)^3 = \mathrm{id}. Since it also has writhe = 3 \cdot 1 + 3 \cdot (-1) = 0, the one-dimensional characters satisfy \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = \chi^{(1^3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1 exactly. At q = 1 (i.e. h = 0), the standard character evaluates to \chi^{(2,1)}(\mathrm{id}) = d_{(2,1)} = 2.

Fact 3 (Borromean-specific). The standard character has no h^2 term: \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6.

Combining: write \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda and take the h^2 coefficient. It is

  \sum_\lambda \bigl[h^2\bigr] y_\lambda \cdot \chi^\lambda\big|_{h=0}
  \;+\; \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\big|_{h=0} \cdot \bigl[h^2\bigr] \chi^\lambda .

The first sum is \sum_\lambda [h^2]y_\lambda \cdot d_\lambda = 0 by Facts 1 and 2. In the second sum the one-dimensional characters are constant, so only y_{(2,1)}|_{h=0} \cdot [h^2]\chi^{(2,1)} survives, and it vanishes by Fact 3.

Generalization: conditions for h^2 = 0

The argument needs three conditions on \beta \in B_n:

  1. Pure braid: \pi(\beta) = \mathrm{id} \in S_n (so \chi^\lambda(\beta)|_{q=1} = d_\lambda for all \lambda).
  2. Writhe zero: equal positive and negative crossings (so 1-dimensional characters are identically 1).
  3. No h^2 term in the multi-dimensional characters: [h^2]\chi^\lambda(\beta) = 0 for every \lambda with y_\lambda|_{h=0} \neq 0 and d_\lambda > 1.

Conditions 1 and 2 alone do not suffice, even at H_3. The pure, writhe-zero braid \sigma_1^2 \sigma_2^{-2} has \chi^{(2,1)} = 2 + 3h^2 + h^4 and \mathrm{tr}_M = 1 + \tfrac34 h^2 + O(h^4) at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1).

Cross-isotope verification: the deuteron (H_6), tritium (H_9), and {}^3\mathrm{He} (H_9) atom braids have h^2 \ne 0 (12.7, 18.7, 36.6 respectively). The three conditions are sufficient for every n, so each of these braids violates at least one of them.
prop:borromean-two-photon-factorisation:
Proposition The Borromean braid is a product of two commuting photons in H_3(q). Let A be an algebra over a commutative ring, and let \sigma_0, \sigma_1 \in A satisfy the relations of H_3(q): \sigma_i^2 = h\,\sigma_i + 1 and \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1, where h = q - q^{-1}. Put V = \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_0\sigma_1 - h\,\sigma_0. Then

  V^3 = 1 + h^2 V - h^2 V^2,
  \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
  (V - 1)\bigl(V^2 + (1 + h^2)V + 1\bigr) = 0,

and

  (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 = (1 + q h V)\,(1 - q^{-1} h V).

Each factor is a photon \gamma(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01}) = 1 + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} that carries only its vertex term:

  1 + q h V = \gamma(0,\, 0,\, q h),
  \qquad
  1 - q^{-1} h V = \gamma(0,\, 0,\, -q^{-1} h),

so (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 = \gamma(0,0,qh)\,\gamma(0,0,-q^{-1}h). In the normal-form basis these are 1 - q h^2\,\sigma_0 + q h\,\sigma_0\sigma_1 and 1 + q^{-1} h^2\,\sigma_0 - q^{-1} h\,\sigma_0\sigma_1.

The two factors commute.

Proof. In the right-associated words of \sigma_0, \sigma_1, rewrite \sigma_0\sigma_0 \mapsto h\sigma_0 + 1, \sigma_1\sigma_1 \mapsto h\sigma_1 + 1 and \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 \mapsto \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0. This gives

  V^2 = \sigma_1\sigma_0 - h^2\,\sigma_0\sigma_1 - h\,\sigma_1 + h^3\,\sigma_0 + h^2,
  V^3 = -h^2\,\sigma_1\sigma_0 + h^3\,\sigma_1 + (1 - h^4) + (h^4 + h^2)\,\sigma_0\sigma_1 - (h^5 + h^3)\,\sigma_0 ,

and comparing the two gives the cubic relation. The product of the two factors is 1 + (q - q^{-1}) h V - h^2 V^2 = 1 + h^2 V - h^2 V^2. The factors are polynomials in V, so they commute. \square

The statement and its proof hold in every algebra that satisfies the relations, so it holds in H_3(q) itself and in each of its representations. It uses no division, no ordering and no value of q.

Relation to the braid used for \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}). In the closed-form proposition the braid is written (\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_2)^3 with generators numbered from 1. Relabelled to \sigma_0, \sigma_1, that is (\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1)^3. The flip \sigma_0 \leftrightarrow \sigma_1 (conjugation by the half twist) sends it to (\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0)^3 = \sigma_1^{-1}(\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3\sigma_1. So the two braids are conjugate and have the same Markov trace. The identity above is for (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3.

Scope. The identity says that \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}, read as a Hecke element, is a product of two photons, each reduced to its vertex term, with weights set by the two eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma_i. It does not select \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}: products of two such photons reach almost every element of H_3(q). It changes no number. Because the two factors commute, the order of the photons cannot distinguish the proton from the neutron.
prop:trace-flavour-no-go:
Proposition A cyclic trace on H_3(q) cannot separate a nucleon word from its flip–reversal. Let A be an algebra over a commutative ring R generated by \sigma_0, \sigma_1 subject to the relations of H_3(q), with h = q - q^{-1}. Let t : A \to R be R-linear with t(xy) = t(yx). Let \theta be the anti-automorphism that exchanges \sigma_0 \leftrightarrow \sigma_1 and reverses products. For every product x = f_1 \cdots f_m of factors f_k = \alpha_k + \beta_k \sigma_{i_k},

  t(\theta(x)) = t(x).

The factors include \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h, every typed crossing operator C(f, f'; \sigma_i) of the typed crossing operator, and their inverses. A Markov trace is such a t.

Proof. The exchange is inner. With \Delta = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0, the braid relation gives \Delta\sigma_0 = \sigma_1\Delta and \Delta\sigma_1 = \sigma_0\Delta, and \Delta is invertible with inverse \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}. So t of the exchanged product equals t(\Delta x \Delta^{-1}) = t(x).

For reversal, every product of factors reduces to a combination of the six elements 1, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \sigma_0\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_0, \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0. The relations \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 and \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 read the same backwards. Multiplying on the right in the original order and on the left in the reversed order therefore produces the same coefficients, with \sigma_0\sigma_1 and \sigma_1\sigma_0 exchanged. A cyclic trace gives t(\sigma_0\sigma_1) = t(\sigma_1\sigma_0). \square

Consequence. Every typed nucleon word whose flavour assignment is carried to another one by \theta has the same trace as that word. In particular this holds for the six placements of the odd quark on (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3. A difference between proton and neutron therefore requires an ingredient that is not a cyclic trace of such a product.

Three smaller statements also hold:

  • the photon \gamma(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01}) = 1 + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} equals 1 + (\varphi_0 - h\varphi_{01})\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1, so the earlier form with last term \sigma_0\sigma_1 is the same family of elements in other coordinates, and the two factors of the two-photon factorisation are photons with only their last term;
  • commuting separators can be moved past a photon;
  • on a 2 \times 2 representation in which \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} has no fixed vector and is not a scalar, its trace is -(1 + h^2) and its determinant is 1.
prop:h3-markov-wenzl-weights:
Proposition Closed-form Jones/Temperley–Lieb weights on H_3(q) (Borromean Jones polynomial): y_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3, y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2, y_{(1^3)} = 0. Let y_\lambda(q) denote the coefficient of \chi^\lambda in the Frobenius expansion \mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{Jones}} = \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} y_\lambda \, \chi^\lambda of the Jones-normalised Markov trace on \mathrm{H}_3(q) — the V_{\mathrm{Jones}} / [2]_q^{\,c-1} Temperley–Lieb closure of Borromean Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6)/(h^2 + 4), i.e. the trace computing the Borromean rings' Jones polynomial. (This is not the full-Hecke Ocneanu trace consumed by the mass/binding pipeline — see the Scope note below.) Then for all q:

  \boxed{\;\;
  y_{(3)}(q) \;=\; \frac{[4]_q}{[2]_q^{3}},
  \qquad
  y_{(2,1)}(q) \;=\; \frac{1}{[2]_q^{2}},
  \qquad
  y_{(1^3)}(q) \;=\; 0.
  \;\;}

At the symmetric point q = 1 these evaluate to

  \bigl(y_{(3)},\, y_{(2,1)},\, y_{(1^3)}\bigr)\big|_{q=1}
  \;=\;
  \bigl(\tfrac{1}{2},\, \tfrac{1}{4},\, 0\bigr)
  \qquad \text{— \emph{not} uniform.}

The scope of this trace normalisation, the immediate Borromean corollary, the chirality of the weights, the notation distinctions, and the significance for the Borromean derivation are collected in the Wenzl-weights context.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:h3-markov-wenzl-weights:
Proof Proof of h3 markov wenzl weights. Three steps, each forced.

Step 1 — y_{(1^3)} \equiv 0 (Temperley–Lieb quotient). The Jones polynomial factors through the Temperley–Lieb algebra \mathrm{TL}_n(q) (Kauffman bracket), which is the quotient of \mathrm{H}_n(q) annihilating every V_\lambda with more than two rows. For n = 3 the only such partition is (1^3), so the Jones-normalised Markov trace assigns it weight zero identically in q. Equivalently, the vanishing is the algebraic identity

  [2]_q^{3} - 2\,[2]_q - [4]_q \;=\; 0,

verified by direct expansion: with [2]_q = q + q^{-1}, [2]_q^3 = q^3 + 3q + 3q^{-1} + q^{-3}, so [2]_q^3 - 2[2]_q = q^3 + q + q^{-1} + q^{-3} = [4]_q.

Step 2 — Markov normalisation. \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}_3) = 1 (the identity braid closes to the 3-component unlink, whose Jones value is exactly the normalising [2]_q^2). With d_{(3)}, d_{(2,1)}, d_{(1^3)} = 1, 2, 1 and Step 1:

  y_{(3)}(q) + 2\, y_{(2,1)}(q) \;=\; 1.

Step 3 — uniqueness from the Borromean closed form. For \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} (writhe 0, image \mathrm{id} \in S_3), \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1 exactly and \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6 with h = q - q^{-1}. Substituting Steps 1–2:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  1 + y_{(2,1)}(q)\,\bigl(\chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) - 2\bigr)
  \;=\;
  1 - y_{(2,1)}(q)\,\bigl(3h^4 + h^6\bigr).

Comparing with the closed form \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6)/(h^2+4) = 1 - (3h^4 + h^6)/(h^2 + 4), and noting 3h^4 + h^6 \neq 0 for h \neq 0:

  y_{(2,1)}(q) \;=\; \frac{1}{h^2 + 4} \;=\; \frac{1}{[2]_q^{2}}
  \qquad\text{(uniquely, for all } q \neq 1\text{; at } q = 1 \text{ by continuity)}.

Then Step 2 gives y_{(3)} = 1 - 2/[2]_q^2 = ([2]_q^2 - 2)/[2]_q^2 = [4]_q / [2]_q^3 using Step 1's identity. \square

Direction of the argument. Step 3 determines y_{(2,1)} from the Borromean closed form, which already uses the Jones–Temperley–Lieb parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1). The step is therefore an internal consistency computation at z = q^3/(q^2+1) rather than an independent selection of z over other members of the Ocneanu trace family — reading it as a selection argument would be circular. The independent characterisation of z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the Temperley–Lieb uniqueness argument (y_{(1^3)}(z) = 0 has the unique non-trivial root z = q^3/(q^2+1)), whose premise — that the relevant fibre functor lands in \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) \simeq \mathrm{TL}_3 — is a separate question.
